s.t: The voice on it isn't Baltimora's frontman Jimmy McShane but its producer Maurizio Bassi: McShane mimed, and nobody dared reveal it while he was alive.
s.src: Culture Sonar: The One-Hit Wonder File: Tarzan Boy
s.q: the voice that rises over the synthesizers is not McShane but Maurizio Bassi ... none had dared share the truth of his lip-synching during the dancer's lifetime

s.t: The Prague ice hockey club HC Sparta Praha has played the chorus of Baltimora's ‘Tarzan Boy’ at home games every time it scores a goal since the 1986–87 season.
s.q: Czech Extraliga team HC Sparta Praha has used the chorus of the song regularly since the 1986–1987 season in its home arenas as their official goal song, played each time the team scores a goal.

s.t: AEW's president Tony Khan bought the rights to Baltimora's ‘Tarzan Boy’ as the entrance music of the wrestler Jungle Boy, tweeting: “Merry Christmas, Jack.”
s.src: Wrestling Inc: Tony Khan on buying rights to Tarzan Boy for Jungle Boy
s.q: Yes, I bought the rights to Tarzan Boy for @boy_myth_legend's entrance. Merry Christmas, Jack.

s.t: With it a hit in 1985, Baltimora's Jimmy McShane told the Manchester Evening News it was “pure novelty”, insisting: “I'm a serious musician and singer… I'm not a novelty merchant!”
s.q: It's pure novelty. ... but I'm a serious musician and singer. I sing all kinds of music – I'm not a novelty merchant!

s.t: The 1989 Bollywood film Maine Pyar Kiya borrowed from Baltimora: its song ‘Aaya Mausam Dosti Ka’ uses a riff lifted from ‘Tarzan Boy’ as its prelude and interlude.
s.src: Odisha Bytes: Maine Pyar Kiya, a landmark movie, its inspired songs
s.q: too features a guitar riff used as a prelude and interlude ... the song “Tarzan Boy” by Baltimora from the album “Living in the Background”

f.t: They got their name when Jimmy McShane shut his eyes and put a finger on a map of the United States: it landed on Baltimore, given an Italian ‘a’.
f.q: McShane took a map of the United States, closed his eyes and happened to place his finger on Baltimore. They changed the final letter to an 'a' to make the name more in keeping with the act's Italian roots.

f.t: Their frontman Jimmy McShane was working as a Red Cross nurse when he was offered the job of being the band's face and body, and dropped everything.
f.q: in quel momento faceva l’infermiere alla Croce rossa ... mollò tutto quando gli proposero di diventare il volto e il corpo di Baltimora.

f.t: Before Baltimora, Jimmy McShane sang the “robotic” backing vocals on Dee D. Jackson's 1978 hit ‘Automatic Lover’, then toured Europe for 18 months as her stage dancer.
f.q: provided the "robotic" backing vocals on her 1978 hit ... toured Europe for 18 months as a stage dancer and backing singer with Jackson and her band.

f.t: On their second single, ‘Woody Boogie’, the keyboards imitate the unmistakable call of the cartoon bird Woody Woodpecker.
f.q: in Woody boogie le tastiere imitavano l’inconfondibile verso del picchio Woody Woodpecker

nf.t: The frontman only mimed: the producer sang it, a secret kept past the frontman's death.
nf.src: Culture Sonar: The One-Hit Wonder File: Tarzan Boy
nf.q: the voice that rises over the synthesizers is not McShane but Maurizio Bassi ... none had dared share the truth of his lip-synching during the dancer's lifetime

3movPj8XYDqzxth2Dv3ma9.title: Impressively Average

s.t: Brigitte Calls Me Baby’s singer Wes Leavins called it ‘a bit of a self-loathing song’, about trying to cope with someone’s very high expectations of you.
s.src: Shore Fire Media: Brigitte Calls Me Baby bio
s.q: a bit of a self-loathing song, about trying to cope with someone’s very high expectations of you

s.t: Brigitte Calls Me Baby first put it out themselves in September 2022; after ATO Records signed them, they pulled it from streaming services and released it again in November 2023.
s.q: The band independently released singles "Impressively Average" and "Eddie My Love" in September 2022 and January 2023, respectively. ... After signing with ATO Records, the band removed "Impressively Average" and This House Is Made of Corners from streaming services to be rereleased in November 2023 under the label.

s.t: Wes Leavins of Brigitte Calls Me Baby says its big, bellowing vocal ending was a spontaneous decision, after producer Dave Cobb inspired him to take more risks.
s.src: Chicago magazine: The Swift Rise of Brigitte Calls Me Baby
s.q: Cobb inspired Leavins to take more risks musically and push his boundaries. The outgrowth of that can be heard on “Impressively Average.” “The big vocal ending was a spontaneous decision,” Leavins says of the song’s anthemic, bellowing climax.

f.t: Their name comes from a high-school English project: singer Wes Leavins wrote to Brigitte Bardot, and they became ‘light pen pals’, writing back and forth a handful of times.
f.src: The Current: interview with Wes Leavins
f.q: I wrote to Brigitte Bardot, and we sort of became light pen pals. We wrote back and forth a handful of times, and when it came time to need a name for the band, it just... hit.

f.t: Singer Wes Leavins was asked to be Elvis Presley’s voice in Baz Luhrmann’s Elvis; when Austin Butler proved he could do it, Leavins played acoustic guitar in pre-production instead.
f.q: Leavins was asked to work on the biopic Elvis to be the voice of Elvis Presley. When Luhrmann found out Austin Butler could emulate Elvis's voice, Wes continued to help by playing acoustic guitar in pre-production.

f.t: Producer Dave Cobb’s best advice to singer Wes Leavins: play each new song over Molly Ringwald’s Breakfast Club dance; if the tempo matches, the whole room should dance.
f.src: DIY: Get To Know… Brigitte Calls Me Baby
f.q: any song you write, play it while you watch Molly Ringwald's dance scene from The Breakfast Club. If the tempo lines up with her movements, you're almost sure to make the entire room dance!

f.t: Their fourth gig ever was opening for Muse at the 2,500-seat Riviera Theater; ‘That was mind-blowing,’ said singer Wes Leavins.
f.src: Rolling Stone Canada: Brigitte Calls Me Baby interview
f.q: a spot opening for Muse at the 2,500-seat Riviera Theater ... “That was mind-blowing because it was our fourth gig,”

f.t: To build breath control, singer Wes Leavins sings while running on a treadmill until he’s out of breath: he wants to fill a room with his voice without a microphone.
f.src: Clash: Next Wave #1182: Brigitte Calls Me Baby
f.q: I like to run and sing. I'll get on a treadmill and sing so that I'm out of breath.
